title: Insurance barriers and trial-and-error psychiatric prescribing
bottleneck: Formularies, prior authorizations, and step therapy force clinicians to prescribe the cheapest drug first rather than the best-fit one, then document failure before better options are covered. This institutionalizes trial-and-error prescribing and delays effective treatment by months.
why_it_blocks: Payer delays worsen symptoms, work performance, and ER risk while forcing clinicians into inefficient, demoralizing care. The financing layer actively degrades the clinical layer.
current_state: Clinicians navigate formularies with 14-day check-ins and PHQ-9 data to justify better medications. Parity laws exist but are weakly enforced; prior authorization reform is slow. State parity-enforcement actions have recovered millions in wrongly denied claims, but proactive auditing remains rare, so most violations go unchallenged. Automated prior-authorization reforms and real-time benefit checks are proposed fixes, but implementation timelines stretch years.
